Tags.rationale: BowlbugsNormal.cs:31 declares EncounterTag.Workers (single element). The sim's `Encounter` dataclass carries no `tags` field of its own -- tag-based no-repeat picking is modeled one layer up, at the room/act picker (`rooms.py`'s `ActRooms.tags` + `_add_without_repeating_tags`/`RoomSet._grab_without_repeating_tags`, seam/rooms_and_map's territory). `_hive_rooms()` pins `"bowlbugs_normal": ("workers",)`, matching the single C# tag by name and count. Cross-referencing seam/rooms_and_map for the picker's own fidelity; this record only verifies the tag VALUE the encounter declares is transcribed correctly.

RoomType.rationale: BowlbugsNormal.cs:33 => RoomType.Monster. The sim has no `room_type` field on `Encounter` either; RoomType is instead encoded by which pool tuple the act places the key in (`normal_keys`, not `weak_keys`/`elite_keys`/`boss_keys`), which the run layer reads to pass the matching `RoomType.MONSTER` into `CombatState.room_type` at combat creation. Verified: "bowlbugs_normal" is in `_hive_rooms().normal_keys` and nowhere else. The dynamic wiring of that pool classification into `CombatState.room_type` at combat-creation time is seam/rooms_and_map's scope, not re-verified here.

HasScene.maps_to: no counterpart -- sim is headless, no Godot scene graph
HasScene.rationale: BowlbugsNormal.cs:35 => true, gating `EncounterModel.ScenePath`/`CreateScene()` (a Godot `PackedScene` instantiation for this encounter's bespoke battle layout). The sim never renders a scene of any kind; there is no headless equivalent and no gameplay-observable consequence -- `HasScene` has exactly one consumer (`GetAssetPaths`'s scene-preload set) and it is purely a rendering asset list.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: BowlbugsNormal.cs:37-52 declares the superset {BowlbugEgg, BowlbugSilk, BowlbugNectar, BowlbugRock} -- exactly the four classes GenerateMonsters can ever draw from, so the C# declaration and the sim's actual roster space already agree. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass has no analogous per-encounter superset field (`BowlbugsNormalEncounter.monster_classes` is an unused vestige of the dataclass, left at its default empty list, since the override replaces `create_monsters` entirely). Traced every consumer of the C# property to see what that costs: `EncounterModel.AllPossibleMonsters` -> `ActModel.AllMonsters` (ActModel.cs:169) -> `ModelDb.Monsters` (ModelDb.cs:177) -> only two readers in the whole tree, `UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68,147` (dev-console `unlock monsters` listing) and `NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164` (bestiary completion-ratio stat) -- both debug/UI surfaces absent from this headless sim. Separately, the one place the sim DOES need a monster-identity vocabulary (`full_env.py`'s `MONSTER_IDS`) is built by `_monster_classes()`, a class-hierarchy walk that already finds BowlbugEgg/Silk/Nectar/Rock via the module import regardless of any per-encounter list. Cost: none observed.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: BowlbugsNormal.cs:54-72: BowlbugRock is appended first with NO draw (`span[0]`, a direct assignment); then, for i in 0..1 (2 iterations), `items` is recomputed each pass as `_workerValidCounts.Keys` (declaration order Egg, Silk, Nectar) filtered to types not yet at their cap of 1, `base.Rng.NextItem(items)` draws once, and the result is appended. Net: 1 fixed monster + exactly 2 draws off the per-encounter Rng, sampling WITHOUT replacement from {Egg, Silk, Nectar}, draw-then-append each time. `bowlbugs.py`'s `BowlbugsNormalEncounter.create_monsters` reproduces this exactly: `monsters=[BowlbugRock(...)]` first with no draw, then a `for _ in range(2)` loop drawing `selection_rng.next_item(candidates)` (parity) from a `candidates` list built in the same [Egg, Silk, Nectar] order and shrunk via `candidates.remove(worker_cls)` after each draw -- the same without-replacement semantics as recomputing the C# LINQ filter each pass, same 2-draw count, same draw-before-append order. Roster, order (Rock, worker1, worker2), composition rule, and draw count all match. Slot strings ("first"/"middle"/"last") are attached to the C# tuples but `BowlbugsNormal` does not override `Slots` (stays `Array.Empty<string>()`), so `CombatManager.cs:848-850`'s `SortEnemiesBySlotName` (CombatState.cs:495-501, `Encounter.Slots.IndexOf(SlotName)`) has an empty row to sort against and is a no-op regardless of which SlotName string a creature carries; grepping every C# consumer of `Creature.SlotName` (CombatManager/CombatState/EncounterModel plus seven monster/power files) turns up none among BowlbugRock/Egg/Silk/Nectar's own move logic, so the slot STRING itself has no gameplay reader for this unit. The sim's `create_monsters` override does not assign `monster.slot_name` at all, which reproduces the only thing that is actually observable here: enemy-list ORDER, which matches.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:39 `ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (not overridden by the sealed `BowlbugsNormal`) -- the encounter object itself is never a hook listener. The sim's `Encounter` is a plain dataclass; `combat.py`'s `CombatState.__init__` stores `self.encounter` for provenance/slot lookups only and never registers it with `HookSystem`, unlike cards/relics/potions/monsters which are each explicitly `hooks.register(...)`-ed. No sim listener exists to diverge.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by BowlbugsNormal
guards.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:64-100: RoomType.Monster => 10-20 gold (x0.75 under Poverty, out of scope per audit rules), scaled by `CalculateGoldProportion` for escapes. `rewards.py:170-173`'s `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] = (10, 20)` matches the non-ascension baseline exactly; `rewards.py:32` documents the ascension/Poverty scaling as deliberately out of scope, consistent with the audit prompt's own scope note. `ShouldGiveRewards` defaults `true` (EncounterModel.cs:62, not overridden); `monsters/base.py`'s `Encounter.should_give_rewards: bool = True` default matches, and `BOWLBUGS_NORMAL = BowlbugsNormalEncounter(id="bowlbugs_normal")` does not override it.
